newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba frees repo business from reserve requirement.
newsitem.headline: Buba frees repo business from reserve requirement.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday it would exempt repurchase agreements with maturities of up to one year from minimum reserve requirements from January 1, 1997, in a widely-expected step designed to enhance Germany's stature as a financial centre.
In a statement the Bundesbank said "the exemption of repo business with maturities of up to one year from the minimum reserve will strengthen the efficiency and competitiveness of the German market."
The Bundesbank said its decision to free up repos with maturities of up to one year will only lead to a small cut in the overall minimum reserve requirement.

Commercial banks have long lobbied the Bundesbank to abolish its requirement that reserves must be held on repurchase agreements conducted between credit institutions or banks and non-banks as this hurt German banks' competitiveness.
In a statement the central bank said it still viewed minimum reserves as an important monetary instrument and would continue to push for their use by the future European Central Bank.
Officially the new ruling will be effective January 1, 1997 but the Bundesbank said that banks need not take the repos into account for their reserve holdings from December 16, 1996.
